stem.text: The Young modulus of steel is twice that of copper.

A $50\,\text{cm}$ length of copper wire of diameter $2.0\,\text{mm}$ is joined to a $50\,\text{cm}$ length of steel wire of diameter $1.0\,\text{mm}$, making a combination wire of length $1.0\,\text{m}$, as shown.

stem.alt: A fixed horizontal support at the top with a vertical combination wire hanging from it. The upper section is a dark thick wire labelled copper wire; the lower section is a thinner wire labelled steel wire. A weight is attached at the bottom of the wire and is labelled weight.

stem.text: The combination wire is stretched by a weight added to its end. Both the copper and the steel wires obey Hooke’s law.
What is the ratio $\dfrac{\text{extension of steel wire}}{\text{extension of copper wire}}$?
